purpose: 以已校正空间关系的基础图为依据，简化图面并补齐风铃；四版同一地理骨架。

jobs.name: 地图01_近岸小环线
jobs.prompt:
Use case: infographic-diagram.
Input: this is an ILLUSTRATIVE LAYOUT DRAFT used only for geography. Transform it into a MUCH SIMPLER LANDSCAPE ARCHITECT'S TOP-DOWN SITE PLAN / GAME BLOCKOUT DIAGRAM.
Output one square map. Strict 90-degree straight-down view. Flat orthographic plan symbols, no visible wall facades, tree trunks, perspective or decorative illustration. Think a clean planning-board diagram drawn from rectangles, smooth irregular polygons, lines and circles. At least 60 percent of the surface is calm untextured solid color. FEWER THAN 12 total woodland blobs. No leaf edges, bark, grass marks, water ripples, surface speckle, realistic shade, flowers, shadows or scattered small props. Clear warm off-white background; light sage open ground; flat pale blue pond; dark muted sage woodland BLOCKS; tan walkable routes; very pale ochre hill. One to three thin contour loops only where the hill is.
Required geography from the draft:
A cottage on the WEST shore of ONE pond, with its EAST WALL almost touching water; the narrow bank/yard is less than HALF the house's width. Keep cottage roughly at (30%,60%), one irregular pond center (58%,55%), old-tree courtyard B around (22%,33%), animal clearing C on the NORTH bank around (60%,27%), hill D at SOUTHEAST around (84%,81%). Cottage is a little brown top-down roof RECTANGLE, no roof tile texture, no wall facade. One rounded canopy beside it.
B is an adjacent compact shared courtyard with one large old-tree canopy symbol, a short two-post drying-rack symbol and small moss-bed oval. Rack and moss bed both border the same open standing area. Its tree is reachable via a very short path from the cottage. C is a clearing on the SAME pond, never a second pond or water separated from A. D is an open low grassy hill with a clearly visible small brown WIND-CHIME symbol (one short crosspiece and three hanging marks) placed at the crest. DO INCLUDE the chime; the current draft omitted it.
Simple gameplay guidance:
Tan route A -> B -> C along north bank -> gentle east-bank climb -> D, then south-bank shoreline return to A. Make routes continuous dry land, wide enough for walking; no water crossing. Orange SMALL arrowheads show outbound A-B-C-D. Purple SMALL arrowheads show return D-A. Two thin blue DASHED sightlines start at D and end specifically at A's roof and at open pond water; they should visibly encode seeing HOME AND WATER together. Keep that diagonal view corridor free of tall woodland blobs. A woodland screen beside the uphill route can end before the crest to make a reveal. No invisible walls or gates.
Labels: exactly four plain bold dark letters A, B, C, D, once each, in their area. No circular letter badges. No extra text, numerals, keys, legend or compass. All objects symbolic and spare. The map should remain readable as a planning diagram at small size. Keep geographic adjacency even when changing enclosure or elevation in the specific option below.
OPTION 1 — BASELINE SHORE LOOP: Follow the locked arrangement closely. B is an open but sheltered courtyard. A->B is the shortest leg, B->C a gentle curve along the northwest pond rim, C->D follows the eastern shore uphill, D->A follows the southern shore home. Keep the pond visually dominant enough to connect the areas, but not oversized. A's short bank apron faces the water. The main differentiator is maximum clarity, a compact learning zone and a single legible scenic loop. Only 6–8 broad woodland patches total. Render about 30–40 simple graphic shapes total, not a dense forest illustration.
